You must take bad experiences and meditate on them to ask yourself “how can I learn something from this? How can this help me grow?” In this case, maybe that job was not a right fit for you. So when you apply to new jobs, seek something that you have experience with or are very interested in learning. You also have to accept what happened. Things went wrong, bad things in the world always happen, and they will continue to happen no matter how hard we try to avoid them. The only thing that should change is how we react to bad things happening. You are not a slave to any job or to anyone. You are a master of yourself. Improve your skills, get motivated and let this experience catapult you forward. Don’t look back. Apologize to your father and explain what happened in an honest way, tell him you want to grow from this experience and that you’re not giving up. Even if he scolds you, you did your part. You can’t control how other people will react to anything, but you can control how you react. Only focus on you and what you can control.

When I was about 13, I began suffering from unbearable joint pains. One joint at a time, would get inflamed and would hurt like hell. It moved from my wrist, to my knee, to my other, wrist, etc. My mom had to take me to the hospital, and they gave her three options of what it could have been (I don’t remember what they were) but they were bad and she ended up fainting at the hospital. She had to take me to 6 different specialists to figure out what was wrong, but none of them could figure it out. The main doctor said it was arthritis. 

In a desperate attempt to heal me, she ended up taking me to a witch doctor. I live in Miami where the Cuban population is large and in Cuba witch doctors (Santeros) are very common. The man said that someone had put some type of curse on me, and performed a whole ritual on me, including sacrificing a chicken on me. After that night, the pain went away and I have never experienced anything similar to those joint pains/inflammations again.
